category: モデルの構築・デプロイ・監視
title: Input Changes During Inference
prompt: Detect daily whether the distribution of applicant features at a real-time endpoint has changed from the training distribution. The labels for approval outcomes will not be available until one month later. What is the best monitoring approach when using data capture?

choices.text: Monitor only the distribution of prediction scores
choices.explanation: This shows output changes but cannot directly determine deviations in individual input features.

choices.text: Monitor only the endpoint CPU utilization
choices.explanation: Changes in the input feature distribution cannot be determined from CPU values.

choices.text: Use Model Monitor to compare a data-quality baseline with inputs in production
choices.explanation: This allows changes in input statistics to be checked without labels.

choices.text: Measure only model accuracy in production
choices.explanation: Measurement requires the correct labels corresponding to the predictions.

learning.reason: Input statistics can be checked without labels.
learning.concept: Data drift and degradation in prediction quality are different. Combine monitoring methods based on the data that is available.

category: モデルの構築・デプロイ・監視
title: Automating Training and Evaluation
prompt: For each new dataset, run preprocessing, training, and evaluation. Register the model only when the evaluation result exceeds a threshold. Automating deployment for inference is not required, but a reproducible workflow is needed.

choices.text: Register the model unconditionally and evaluate it afterward
choices.explanation: Models that fail to meet the criterion are also registered.

choices.text: Steps and conditional branches in SageMaker Pipelines
choices.explanation: The evaluation result can be used as a condition to run subsequent model registration.

choices.text: Auto scaling for the inference endpoint
choices.explanation: This controls inference capacity; it is not a model-evaluation workflow.

choices.text: Manage only the version numbers in Model Registry
choices.explanation: This manages models after registration and does not automate preprocessing or training.

learning.reason: The evaluation result can be used as a condition for subsequent model registration.
learning.concept: Recording the data, training configuration, evaluation metrics, and model version helps ensure reproducibility.

category: モデルの構築・デプロイ・監視
title: Large-Scale Overnight Inference
prompt: The inputs and results are in S3, and millions of inferences must be run in a batch overnight. No HTTP endpoint for real-time requests should be created, and the results will be aggregated after the job completes. Which inference method should be selected to minimize operational overhead?

choices.text: Start a training job for each input
choices.explanation: Only inference is required, so retraining the model is unnecessary.

choices.text: Send individual requests with SageMaker Asynchronous Inference
choices.explanation: This can scale, but it requires an endpoint and a design that sends a request for each input.

choices.text: SageMaker Batch Transform
choices.explanation: It can run a job on inputs in S3 and save the results to S3.

choices.text: Keep a SageMaker real-time endpoint running continuously
choices.explanation: This is suitable for low-latency synchronous responses, but continuously running resources are unnecessary for this overnight batch.

learning.reason: It can run a job on inputs in S3 and save the results to S3.
learning.concept: Choose an inference method by separating the latency requirements of synchronous APIs from the throughput requirements of processing data in bulk.

category: モデルの構築・デプロイ・監視
title: Training and Inference Consistency for Features
prompt: Multiple models calculate the same customer features each time. Online prediction requires low-latency retrieval of the latest values, while training requires historical data. Which feature is suitable for reusing the feature definitions and values?

choices.text: SageMaker Feature Store
choices.explanation: It manages shared features and makes them available for both online and offline use.

choices.text: Overwrite only the latest features in a DynamoDB table
choices.explanation: This enables low-latency retrieval but does not retain the overwritten history needed for training.

choices.text: Implement separate calculations in each model's inference code
choices.explanation: This is likely to create differences in formulas and update timing.

choices.text: Reuse only the input text from CloudWatch Logs
choices.explanation: This does not provide unified feature definitions or low-latency retrieval.

learning.reason: It manages shared features and makes them available for both online and offline use.
learning.concept: Online and offline stores do not serve the same role. Freshness and point-in-time consistency must also be considered in the design.

category: モデルの構築・デプロイ・監視
title: Future Information Leaking into Training Data
prompt: On the first day of each month, the organization predicts cancellations through the end of that month. Validation accuracy increased sharply when the post-cancellation refund category was included as a feature. While continuing to select models, what should be changed to evaluate future performance as of the beginning of the month?

choices.text: Limit the features to those available at prediction time and evaluate them using a time-series split
choices.explanation: This removes future information that would not be available during actual inference.

choices.text: Increase the number of model parameters
choices.explanation: This does not remove features that contain future information.

choices.text: Increase the number of random splits while keeping the same features
choices.explanation: Fields unavailable at inference time remain in the data.

choices.text: Hash the refund category and continue using it as an input
choices.explanation: Changing the format does not remove the future information.

learning.reason: This removes future information that would not be available during actual inference.
learning.concept: Check for data leakage based not only on the feature value, but also on when that value became known.

category: モデルの構築・デプロイ・監視
title: Checking for Bias During Training Preparation
prompt: A classifier is being developed using historical loan-approval labels. The team wants to investigate a concern that the proportion of positive labels differs across certain attributes before the model has been trained. What should they use?

choices.text: Compare the model's production CPU utilization
choices.explanation: This does not evaluate the label distribution in the data.

choices.text: Use the pre-training bias metrics in SageMaker Clarify
choices.explanation: These metrics can evaluate attribute-specific patterns in the data.

choices.text: Compare only feature contributions in explanations of the trained model
choices.explanation: Contributions to predictions differ from pre-training bias in the labels themselves.

choices.text: Adjust the maximum size of the inference response
choices.explanation: Changing the response format cannot reveal dataset patterns.

learning.reason: These metrics can evaluate attribute-specific patterns in the data.
learning.concept: Bias in the data and bias visible in model predictions must be checked at different stages.

category: モデルの構築・デプロイ・監視
title: Imbalanced Batch Comparison
prompt: Only 0.3% of the devices targeted for failure prediction actually fail. The maintenance team can investigate a fixed number of top-ranked devices each day, and data from multiple days is available for the same device. Which evaluation best compares the operational effectiveness of the candidates?

choices.text: Compare all models at a threshold of 0.5 and look only at the number of failure predictions
choices.explanation: The output scales differ, and this does not show how many failures were correctly captured.

choices.text: Randomly split the rows and select the model based on overall accuracy
choices.explanation: This makes it difficult to capture generalization to the future and detection effectiveness under the limited investigation capacity.

choices.text: Select the candidate with the highest ROC-AUC on the training data
choices.explanation: This can miss overfitting and does not reflect the daily inspection limit.

choices.text: Use a future period and measure the failure capture rate within the daily top-ranked limit
choices.explanation: This reproduces the time order and investigation capacity and measures how many target failures can be identified.

learning.reason: This reproduces the time order and investigation capacity and measures how many target failures can be identified.
learning.concept: When field action is limited to the top K items, the evaluation must include the same budget constraint.

category: モデルの構築・デプロイ・監視
title: Non-Impacting Comparison of Production Candidates
prompt: The current online inference model is responding to users. You need to measure a candidate's latency using the same input distribution as production, but the candidate's results must never be returned to customers.

choices.text: Switch all traffic to the candidate endpoint and roll back if an issue occurs
choices.explanation: The candidate would determine the responses returned to customers.

choices.text: Use Batch Transform with average inputs from one week ago
choices.explanation: This does not affect customer responses, but it does not directly evaluate the same input distribution as production.

choices.text: Use SageMaker shadow testing to replicate a portion of production inputs to the candidate
choices.explanation: Responses are returned by the current model, while the candidate is evaluated with the same type of production inputs.

choices.text: Make the candidate a production variant with a 10% weight
choices.explanation: The candidate's responses would be returned to some customers.

learning.reason: Responses are returned by the current model, while the candidate is evaluated with the same type of production inputs.
learning.concept: Shadow testing compares models without returning the candidate's responses; canary testing validates a new version by serving it to some users.

category: モデルの構築・デプロイ・監視
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Detecting Sensor-Value Distribution Drift
prompt: A factory's anomaly-detection model has been deployed to another facility. Collecting failure labels takes several weeks, but you need to detect first that temperature and vibration inputs have deviated from the training-time statistics.

choices.text: Set up only model-quality monitoring that uses actual failure labels
choices.explanation: The required labels are not immediately available.

choices.text: Retrain based only on the average prediction score
choices.explanation: This cannot identify the input features causing the change and skips validation of the distribution shift.

choices.text: Sample inference inputs and configure data-quality monitoring against the training-time feature statistics
choices.explanation: This can detect deviations in the input distribution and constraints before the labels are available.

choices.text: Monitor the average CPU utilization of inference
choices.explanation: This shows changes in operational load but not differences in the input distribution.

learning.reason: This can detect deviations in the input distribution and constraints before the labels are available.
learning.concept: Data drift examines inputs, whereas model quality examines the relationship between predictions and observed outcomes. They can be designed as separate alerts.

category: モデルの構築・デプロイ・監視
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Resilience to Interruptions During Long-Running Training
prompt: You are running training in SageMaker that takes half a day. There is sufficient time before the deadline, and the model can resume from an intermediate state. You want to use the tolerance for interruptions to reduce compute costs.

choices.text: Use Managed Spot Training and configure S3 synchronization for checkpoints saved by the training code
choices.explanation: This uses lower-cost capacity and allows training to resume from a saved point after an interruption.

choices.text: Use On-Demand capacity and synchronize the intermediate state to S3
choices.explanation: This protects progress but does not use the interruption tolerance to reduce the price.

choices.text: Use Managed Spot Training without saving checkpoints
choices.explanation: This provides the discount but cannot recover long-running training progress.

choices.text: Place only the final trained model in S3
choices.explanation: The training state at the time of an interruption is not saved.

learning.reason: This uses lower-cost capacity and allows training to resume from a saved point after an interruption.
learning.concept: The training code must save the state required for resumption, such as optimizer state, and resumption from an intermediate point must also be tested.
